transcript:
This is NPR News now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
King tides and powerful waves flooded parts of the Northern California coast on Thanksgiving.
In Pacifica, just south of San Francisco, waves ripped apart a section of the city's
pier earlier this week.
Savannah Peterson lives a few blocks away.
She says the waves washed debris into the streets.
At this point, too much is compromised in front of our homes for me personally to feel
safe.
So I'll be packing up and I hope that a lot of my neighbors have the opportunity to do
the same and stay safe.
On the east coast, damage assessments are underway after a powerful nor'easter hit
on Thanksgiving.
The storm flooded roads and knocked out power to hundreds of thousands of homes and businesses.
Crews in New York City rescued people from flooded cars.
Congress is up against a deadline next month to prevent another partial government shutdown.
NPR's Barbara Sproun reports funding is one of the main issues facing lawmakers when they
return from the Thanksgiving break.
High up on the agenda is funding the government.
Funding is set to expire on December 11.
Congress has to either pass a dozen appropriations bills or approve another stopgap measure,
known as a continuing resolution.
Building a CR would keep the government open and bypass another government shutdown.
The House will decide when to take up a permitting reform package as well, aimed at speeding
up the building of the nation's infrastructure.
The Senate has already passed the measure.
And there's also a leadership election in the Senate, where Democratic senators will
pick their next majority leader.
Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen is challenging New York Senator Chuck Schumer for the top
job.
Barbara Sproun and PR News, Washington.
His families gather over the Thanksgiving holiday.
Many are finding that households look very different from the past, including more homes
where dads are single parenting.
NPR's Brian Mann reports.
The study by the Census Bureau looked at American families and their living arrangements comparing
home life in 2026 with 1976.
The data shows some big changes.
The number of homes where one person lives alone has grown by about a third, now accounting
for more than 40 million households.
Meanwhile, the percentage of families with kids living at home fell sharply from 54 percent
a half century ago to 38 percent this year, though the study showed more than half of
adults aged 18 to 24 now live with their parents.
The nation also saw a rise in single parent households.
Single moms still carry most of the load.
But the census report found homes where single dads care for kids nearly tripled to 19 percent.
There's also a much higher percentage of households occupied by seniors.
Brian Mann, NPR News.
Stocks are trading higher on Wall Street at this hour.
The Dow is up 308 points.
The NASDAQ composite up 170.
This is NPR News.
Voters in Spain go to the polls on Sunday in an early parliamentary election.
Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez is fighting to stay in office eight years into
the job.
News called the election when lawmakers rejected his proposals to tackle Spain's housing crisis.
The latest polls put the conservative People's Party on track to win the most seats.
In eastern France, one red wine gets its own celebration every November.
Rebecca Rossman reports on the annual tradition.
It's called the Fête du Beaujolais Nouveau.
French law dictates that this fruity, slightly acidic red wine cannot be sold before 1201
a.m. on the third Thursday in November.
But just after the stroke of midnight, the 2026 vintage is uncorked.
And the party is on.
The epicenter of celebrations is here in the hilly Beaujolais capital of Beaugeux, where
thousands gather from across France and around the world.
Annual sales of Beaujolais Nouveau have dropped significantly since their peak in the 1990s.
But outside of France, the United States remains one of the top export markets for the drink,
commonly served around the Thanksgiving table.
For NPR News, I'm Rebecca Rossman in Beaujolais, France.
Gas prices in the U.S. are averaging around $3.55 for a gallon of regular.
According to AAA, that's down about $3.69 a week ago last year at this time.
The national average was just over $3 a gallon.
This is NPR News.

topics.text: King tides and powerful waves flood Northern California coast, damaging Pacifica pier on Thanksgiving
Nor'easter floods roads and knocks out power to hundreds of thousands on East Coast
Congress faces December 11 funding deadline to avoid another partial government shutdown
Census data shows rise in one-person households and single fathers, fewer homes with children
Spain holds early parliamentary election Sunday as Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez fights to stay in office
Beaujolais Nouveau wine released at midnight in Beaujolais, France, drawing thousands to celebrate
U.S. gas prices average about $3.55 per gallon, down from a year ago
